anyOf.title: MCPCredentialBinding
anyOf.description:
Where an API-key endpoint's credential goes when the relay sends it.

Configuration only: the value stays in the vault behind the endpoint's `secret_id`, so
this is as readable as `base_url` is. `kind` and `name` match the SDK's
`HeaderCredentialBinding`. A `header` binding sends `<name>: <prefix> <value>`, or
`<name>: <value>` with no prefix; a `query` binding adds `<name>=<value>` to the
upstream URL at request time; a `url` binding puts the value where `base_url` holds
`{secret}`. The stored URL never holds the value. The prefix is the scheme word
(`Bearer`, `Basic`) a server expects in front of the value, because a raw key under
`Authorization` is refused by every server that names a scheme.

Valid combinations: a `header` binding needs `name` and may take `prefix`; a `query`
binding needs `name` and takes no `prefix`; a `url` binding takes neither `name` nor
`prefix`.

schema.title: MCPEndpointProbeRequest
schema.description:
Inspect a server URL before an endpoint exists.

The probe routes a request and reports what came back. It takes no name (nothing is
being labelled), no slug or id (nothing is being identified), and no credential value.

`secret_id` names a project secret to send the way `credential_binding` says, which
is a `{secret}` in the URL's path when it says nothing: that address does not exist
without its key. A key sent in a header or the query is how a changed key is checked
before a connection saves it. The API reads the value from the vault, so the browser
never sends it.
